question: Find all real values of $k$ for which the system $kx+y=2$ and $2x+ky=3$ is consistent with a unique solution. Justify the restriction on $k$.
explanation:
Coefficient matrix
The coefficient matrix of the system is $$A=\begin{bmatrix}k&1\\2&k\end{bmatrix}$$
Determinant calculation
Its determinant is $$|A|=k^2-2$$
Unique-solution condition
The system is consistent with a unique solution when the coefficient matrix is nonsingular. Therefore, $$k^2-2\ne0$$
Restriction on the parameter
The excluded values satisfy $k^2=2$, giving $k=\sqrt{2}$ or $k=-\sqrt{2}$. Hence, the system has a unique solution for $$k\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{-\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2}\}$$
